paper_a.title: On a new proof of the key step in the proof of Brouwer's fixed point theorem

paper_b.title: Two Applications of Topological Fixed Point Theory

metadata.description: Both papers live in the fixed-point-theory family but their substantive content is essentially disjoint. Paper A (Krylov) gives a new analytic proof of the Jacobian-equality lemma underlying Brouwer's fixed point theorem and then derives Brouwer's theorem itself. Paper B (Ambi) treats Brouwer's theorem only as a cited black box and applies topological fixed-point machinery (Gromov compactification, mod-p Lefschetz) to two unrelated problems: Cartan's theorem on finite-order isometries and a prime-divisor constraint on automorphism groups of planar domains. The only genuine alignment is paper A's contribution (Brouwer's theorem) matching paper B's cited prior result; everything else is `none`. The originally hypothesised AP relation does not survive inspection.

matches.explanation: Both nodes state Brouwer's fixed point theorem for the closed unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$: every continuous self-map of $\bar{B}$ has a fixed point. The statements coincide up to notation ($\bar{B}$ vs $\mathbb{B}^n$). This is a paper↔external alignment: paper A *proves* Brouwer (TP463.1, origin: paper) while paper B *cites* it (TP460.4, origin: external) as a tool inside the proof of Cartan's theorem. This is the only nontrivial point of contact between the two papers.

Paper A's proof of Brouwer's theorem (smooth-case retraction obstruction + polynomial approximation of continuous maps) has no counterpart in paper B; paper B uses Brouwer as a black-box citation and never proves or reproves it.
The central Jacobian-integral equality lemma (Lemma 3.21.1) of Krylov's paper has no analogue in paper B, which works topologically and never engages with smooth Jacobians or volume-form arguments.

The paper-A proof of Lemma 3.21.1 — using one-parameter perturbations $F_t = tF + x$, equality of images for small $t$, then polynomial coefficient comparison — is paper-A-specific and absent in paper B.

Paper A's `no-smooth-retraction' corollary (Corollary 3.21.1) is paper-A-specific. Paper B does not invoke or restate any retraction-nonexistence result; its topological pipeline uses Brouwer directly without going through the smooth retraction route.
The proof of the no-retraction corollary (apply Lemma 3.21.1 with $F=\mathrm{id}$, observe $\det DG=0$ since columns of $DG$ are tangent to $\partial\Omega$) has no parallel in paper B.
Paper A's partial-derivative notation $D_i u$ is a setup definition with no analogue in paper B's topological framework.
Paper A's Jacobian-matrix definition $DF$ is central to its analytic proof but paper B never uses Jacobian determinants.
The perturbed-mapping construction $F_t(x) = tF(x) + x$ is paper-A-specific; paper B has no perturbation-of-identity device.
The polynomial-in-$t$ identity $\int \det(tDF+I)\,dx = \int \det(tDG+I)\,dx$ is internal to Krylov's analytic proof and has no counterpart in paper B.

Cartan's fixed point theorem for finite-order isometries of Cartan-Hadamard manifolds is one of paper B's two main contributions. It has no analogue in paper A, which is purely about Brouwer's Euclidean theorem and its analytic key step.
The pencil-of-geodesics corollary (odd-dimensional case) is paper-B-specific, with no analogue in paper A's setting.

The prime-divisor constraint $k^3 \equiv k \bmod p$ for $|\mathrm{Aut}(\Omega_k)|$ is paper B's second main result. Paper A says nothing about complex planar domains, automorphism groups, or number-theoretic constraints.
Paper B's proof of Cartan's theorem (Gromov compactification + Brouwer + horosphere induction) has no counterpart in paper A.
Paper B's proof of the pencil-of-geodesics corollary via mod-$p$ Lefschetz on $\mathbb{R}P^{n-1}$ has no counterpart in paper A.
Paper B's proof of the prime-divisor constraint via the generalised Lefschetz number on $\Omega \setminus \mathrm{Fix}(\sigma)$ (a wedge of circles) has no counterpart in paper A.
The fixed-point cardinality bound $\#\mathrm{Fix}(\sigma) \leq 2$ used inside paper B's planar-domain argument has no analogue in paper A.
The Lefschetz-vanishing congruence $0 = \lambda(\bar{\tau}) \equiv \lambda(\bar{\tau}^p) \bmod p$ is internal to paper B's mod-$p$ argument, with no analogue in paper A.
The Euler-characteristic congruence $\chi(\Omega) = 1 - k - \#\mathrm{Fix}(\sigma) \equiv 0 \bmod p$ is internal to paper B's planar-domain proof, with no counterpart in paper A.
Paper B's open problem on characterising automorphism groups of bounded planar domains has no analogue in paper A.

The definition of a pencil of geodesics (non-intersecting family pairwise within finite Hausdorff distance) is specific to paper B's Cartan-Hadamard setting; paper A has no notion of geodesics or Hausdorff distance.
